newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher with Kinnevik, Volvo up.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher with Kinnevik, Volvo up.

text.p: Swedish shares ended higher on Tuesday on the back of a strong U.S. market.
The exchange's general index rose 1.74 percent to 2,706.76 in turnover of 4.46 billion crowns.

Investment and media group Kinnevik jumped 6.5 crowns to 203.5 after its partly owned cellular telephone operator Millicom International Cellular announced it would spin off and list its Asian operations.
Automotive group Volvo rode on Retail and Wholesale Institute HUI's Monday forecast that new car sales will rise steadily to the year 2003.
The share rose six crowns to 197.

Pharmaceutical company Astra leaped 8.5 crowns to 355.5 crowns rose as investors bought heavyweights. Telecoms group Ericsson jumped six crowns to 260.5 after news it will restructure its Infocom Systems business area.
Car safety equipment company Autoliv kept benefiting from Monday's news that a merger with a Morton unit was ready. The share rose two crowns to 331.
Forestry group SCA also belonged to the winners, up 5.5 to 167.
